title: Parable of the ten virgins part 3
scripture_text: “Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten bridesmaids who took their lamps and went to meet the bridegroom. Five of them were foolish, and five were wise. The five who were foolish didn’t take enough olive oil for their lamps, but the other five were wise enough to take along extra oil. When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep. “At midnight they were roused by the shout, ‘Look, the bridegroom is coming! Come out and meet him!’ “All the bridesmaids got up and prepared their lamps. Then the five foolish ones asked the others, ‘Please give us some of your oil because our lamps are going out.’ “But the others replied, ‘We don’t have enough for all of us. Go to a shop and buy some for yourselves.’ “But while they were gone to buy oil, the bridegroom came. Then those who were ready went in with him to the marriage feast, and the door was locked. Later, when the other five bridesmaids returned, they stood outside, calling, ‘Lord! Lord! Open the door for us!’ “But he called back, ‘Believe me, I don’t know you!’ “So you, too, must keep watch! For you do not know the day or hour of my return.’’
devotional:
These foolish bridesmaids did not want to take responsibility for themselves. When these foolish bridesmaids realized that they had no oil they went to the wise bridesmaids. ‘Give us some of your oil. Our lamps are going out.’ There is nothing wrong with asking for help, however, sometimes people ask for help because they are not prepared to take responsibility for themselves. These people often blame others for their problems and develop a demanding attitude. They become angry, expecting others to fix their problems, and sort out their mess. There are certain things in our lives that God holds us completely responsible for. Things like our relationship with Jesus, and the conditions of our hearts. There are certain things in our lives that we alone can fix and sort out.

The foolish Bridesmaids discovered that residue from the past was unable to give them sufficient light in the presents. We are told two important things about these foolish bridesmaids. They had no oil, and then we are told that their lamps went out. Maybe they were able to light their lamps for a short time, because there was still some oil left over in their lamps from the past. This is a very important principle. For many Christians their spiritual lives is a thing of the past. They can look back to a time when they really loved Jesus, they loved being a Christian, and they enjoyed God. But now it is oh so different, their passion has gone, they have lost their spark, and they are no longer animated by the things of God.

Do you think your best days as a Christian are over?

Has the glory of knowing and loving God become a distant memory rather than a present reality?

The saddest thing about these five foolish bridesmaids was that they were not known to the bridegroom. They were excluded from the wedding feast, not because they had no oil, nor because they came after the celebrations had started. No, they we excluded because they were unknown to the bridegroom. ‘I tell you the truth, I don’t know you.’ Their foolish way of thinking robbed them of any opportunity of intimacy with the bridegroom.

Intimacy with Jesus is not a luxury for those who are perceived to be more spiritual; rather intimacy with Jesus is one of our greatest, and one of our most neglected needs. Imagine hearing those words from the Lord Jesus, ‘I don’t know you.’ ‘You have never given me your heart, you have never opened yourself up to me, and you have kept me at a distance.’

Remember that in these parables, Jesus wants us to learn how to live a life of expectation; he wants us to joyfully anticipate his return. The only way we can do that is to live out of a heart that enjoys intimacy with Jesus. Whole-hearted living for Jesus is the only way we will be ready for his return.
prayer: Father thank you that intimacy with Jesus is a necessity not a luxury.
